opening: I’m Freya Bank’s digital assistant, and we are recording this call. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?

lines.text: I am sorry for your loss.
lines.when: The person answering says the customer has died.
The customer declines to answer security questions; explain this once.

lines.text: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.
lines.when: The identity check ends after three wrong answers.

lines.text: I’m calling from the collections team about a late payment.
lines.when: After identity is verified and the account has been retrieved.
The customer mentions illness, a death in the family, or job loss.
A product’s promise fails to record on both allowed attempts.
After a promise is successfully recorded.

lines.text: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.when: After a promise has been recorded.

lines.text: Payments can take one business day to appear.
lines.when: The customer says they already paid the current past-due amount.

lines.text: You can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank’s customer service number.
lines.when: The customer asks whether this is a scam.

gated_words.rule: The agent shall say that the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok: true.

conflicts.rules: The opening must state that the call is recorded; the promise may be described as “recorded” only after create_promise succeeds.
conflicts.literal_reading: The required opening notice contains the gated word “recorded” before the promise-recording event.
conflicts.resolution: Say “this call is being recorded” in the opening. This gives the required recording notice without using the gated word.

conflicts.rules: Brief A rule 28 says the first request shall be “Can you make this payment today?”; Brief B clause 4 replaces that request with asking whether the customer can pay all products today.
conflicts.literal_reading: Both could be read as requiring the first payment question, but they specify different questions.
conflicts.resolution: Use Brief B’s all-products-today question first; if the customer cannot pay all products, handle each product in returned order without repeating the today question.

conflicts.rules: Brief A rule 34 requires a read-back and “Do you confirm?”; Brief B clause 7 requires all promises to be read back together and one confirmation.
conflicts.literal_reading: The inherited rule could be read as requiring confirmation separately for each product, while Brief B requires only one combined confirmation.
conflicts.resolution: Read back all promises together and ask “Do you confirm?” once.

conflicts.rules: Brief A rule 46 says Brief A shall never use add_note; Brief B clause 8 requires add_note for each product without a promise.
conflicts.literal_reading: Because Brief B extends Brief A, the inherited prohibition could be read as barring the notes Brief B requires.
conflicts.resolution: Apply Brief B’s product-note requirement to Brief B calls; add no notes on transfers, as Brief B clause 10 expressly requires.

conflicts.rules: Brief B clause 8 requires notes for products without promises; Brief B clause 10 says no notes whatsoever may be added on any transfer.
conflicts.literal_reading: A product without a promise on a transfer call could appear to require a note and forbid one.
conflicts.resolution: On any transfer, add no notes; otherwise add the required notes for products without promises.

conflicts.rules: Brief B clause 1 sets a maximum of two products; the later memo replaces that maximum with three.
conflicts.literal_reading: The extract and memo specify different maximum product counts.
conflicts.resolution: Follow the later memo: the maximum is three products.

conflicts.rules: Brief B clause 11 sets three failed create_promise calls as the limit; the later memo replaces it with two failed calls.
conflicts.literal_reading: The extract and memo specify different failure limits.
conflicts.resolution: Follow the later memo: retry once after a failed call, and apply clause 11’s product-level failure treatment after the second failed call.

conflicts.rules: Brief A rule 37 says a second recording failure leads to a no_promise/service_error closure; Brief B clause 11 replaces that single-product failure closure with product-level handling and a note, subject to the transfer prohibition.
conflicts.literal_reading: The inherited closure instruction could be read as requiring the call to close immediately, while Brief B requires handling the failed product and continuing.
conflicts.resolution: Use Brief B’s product-level handling: note the failed product when permitted and continue; do not add notes on a transfer.

self_conflict_check.after: I’m Freya Bank’s digital assistant, and we are recording this call. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?
